summary: The root كَسَدَ (kasada) primarily means something became unsaleable, difficult to sell, or in little demand. It also describes a market becoming stagnant or dull.
lane: 1 كَسَدَ ذ , (S, L, Msb, K,) aor. كَسُدَ , (L, Msb,) inf. n. كَسَادٌ (S, L, Msb, K) and كُسُودٌ ; (K;) and كَسُدَ ; (L, K;) but the former is the verb in common use; (TA;) It (a thing, S, Msb, a commodity, &c., L) was, or became, unsaleable, or difficult of sale, and in little demand. (L, Msb, K.) The original meaning is It was, or became, in a bad, corrupt, or unsound state. (T, Msb.) -A2- كَسَدَتِ السُّوقُ , (aor. كَسُدَ , inf. n. كَسَادٌ , L,) The market was, or became, stagnant, or dull, with respect to traffic. (S, * A, L, Msb, K.) See 4.
